The logic is here is:

Ratio of first number to second number is equal to 1/7.

In the above options, the 2nd number is completely divided by the 1st number.

In option (3), does not follow the pattern.

Hence, pair (18, 128) is an odd one.

questions.question: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the equation correct. 48 * 12 * 8 * 15 * 3 * 44
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the equation correct.

48 * 12 * 8 * 15 * 3 * 44
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule:

Given equation 48 * 12 * 8 * 15 * 3 * 44

Option 1 : Using the combination ×, ÷, =, −, +

48 × 12 ÷ 8 = 15 - 3 + 44

By BODMAS rule

48 × 1.5 = 59 - 3

72 ≠ 56 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : Using combination ÷, ×, +, −, =

48 ÷ 12 × 8 + 15 - 3 = 44

4 × 8 + 15 - 3 = 44

32 + 15 - 3 = 44

47 - 3 = 44

44 = 44 (LHS = RHS)

Option 3 : Using the combination =, ×, +, ÷, −

48 = 12 × 8 + 15 ÷ 3 - 44

48 = 12 × 8 + 5 - 44

48 = 96 + 5 - 44

48 = 101 - 44

48 = 57 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4 : Using the combination +, ÷, −, =, ×

48 + 12 ÷ 8 - 15 = 3 × 44

48 + 1.5 - 15 = 132

49.5 - 15 = 132

34.5 = 132 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is “÷, ×, +, −, =”.

questions.solution:
According to the given information,

Total number of persons present at a press conference = 28.

7 of them refuse to shake hands

Total number of persons who shake hand n = 28 – 7 = 21

The number of handshakes exchanged is,

= n (n - 1) ÷ 2

= 21(21 – 1) ÷ 2

= 21 × 20 ÷ 2

= 21 × 10

= 210

Hence, total number of handshake is “210”

questions.question: Who among the following economists formulated the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU)?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following economists formulated the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is HH Gossen.

Key Points

  • HH Gossen formulated the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU).
    • He formulated this law in 1854.

Important Points

  • Marginal Utility is the change in total utility due to a one-unit change in the level of consumption.
  • Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility
    • It states that as a person consumes an item or a product, the satisfaction or utility that they derive from the product declines as they consume more and more of that product.
    • In other words, the additional utility gained from an increase in consumption decreases with each subsequent increase in the level of consumption.
  • Demand curves are downward-sloping in microeconomic models since each additional unit of a good or service is put toward a less valuable use.
  • Marketers use the law of diminishing marginal utility because they want to keep marginal utility high for products that they sell.

    • The most common gold compounds are auric chloride (AuCl3) and chloroauric acid (HAuCl4).

    • Absorbing water and minerals
      • Thin-walled epidermal cells and root hairs are well suited to absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. The roots of many plants also have a mycorrhizal relationship with fungi for greater absorption.
    • Anchoring and supporting the plant
      • Root systems help anchor plants to the ground, allowing plants to grow tall without toppling over. A tough covering may replace the epidermis in older roots, making them ropelike and even stronger.
    • Storing food
      • In many plants, ground tissues in roots store food produced by the leaves during photosynthesis. The bloodroot stores food in its roots over the winter.

We know if a line from vertex cuts the opposite side in a certain ratio then the area of two new triangles is also divided in that ratio

 \(\text{Area ΔAEB}\over{\text{Area ΔEBD}}\) = \(2\over3\) → (i)

\(\text{Area ΔEBD}\over{\text{Area ΔECD}}\) = \(3\over4\) → (ii) 

From Eqn (I) and (ii), we have

ΔAEB : ΔEBD : ΔECD

    2    :     3     :     4

 \(\text{Area ΔECD}\over{\text{Area ΔAEB}}\) = \(4\over2\) = \(2\over1\) = 2 : 1

∴ The required ratio is 2 : 1

questions.question: In a circle, a ten cm long chord is at a distance of 12 cm from the centre of the circle. The length of the diameter of the circle (in cm) is:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle, a ten cm long chord is at a distance of 12 cm from the centre of the circle. The length of the diameter of the circle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Half of the chord length = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13):

The radius of the circle (r) = 13 cm.

Diameter of the circle = 2 × r = 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the chord (AC) = 10 cm

Distance of the chord from the centre (OM) = 12 cm

Formula Used:

1. The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord: AM = MC = AC ÷ 2

2. Pythagoras Theorem in right-angled triangle ΔAMO: OA2 = AM2 + OM2

3. Diameter of a circle = 2 × Radius (r)

Calculations:

Let O be the centre of the circle and AC be the chord of length 10 cm.

OM is the perpendicular distance from the centre O to the chord AC, so OM = 12 cm.

⇒ AM = AC ÷ 2

⇒ AM = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

In the right-angled triangle ΔAMO, by Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OA2 = AM2 + OM2

⇒ r2 = 52 + 122

⇒ r2 = 25 + 144

⇒ r2 = 169

⇒ r = √169 = 13 cm

Therefore, the radius of the circle is 13 cm.

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 13 = 26 cm

Incorrect Options Explanation:

The value 20 cm is incorrect because it corresponds to a radius of 10 cm, which does not satisfy the Pythagorean relation with a distance of 12 cm.

The value 22 cm is incorrect because it corresponds to a radius of 11 cm, which does not form a valid right-angled triangle with the given dimensions.

The value 13 cm is incorrect because it represents the radius of the circle, whereas the question asks for the diameter.

∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.

Additional Information

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects the chord. Conversely, the line joining the center to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a2 + b2 = c2. Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Equal Chords and Distance

Chords of a circle that are equal in length are equidistant from the center of the circle. Conversely, chords equidistant from the center are equal in length.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 7 : 8. After 6 years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 8 : 9. If C's present age is 10 years more than the present age of A, then the present age (in years) of C is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 7 : 8. After 6 years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 8 : 9. If C's present age is 10 years more than the present age of A, then the present age (in years) of C is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Present ratio of A : B = 7 : 8 and after 6 years ratio = 8 : 9.

The difference in both ratio parts is constant: (8 − 7) = 1 and (9 − 8) = 1.

1 unit → 6 years.

Present age of A = 7 × 6 = 42 years.

Present age of C = 42 + 10 = 52 years.

∴ The correct answer is 52 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Present ratio of A and B = 7 : 8

Ratio after 6 years = 8 : 9

C's present age = A's present age + 10 years

Calculations:

Let the present ages of A and B be 7x and 8x respectively.

⇒ (7x + 6) / (8x + 6) = 8 / 9

⇒ 9 × (7x + 6) = 8 × (8x + 6)

⇒ 63x + 54 = 64x + 48

⇒ 64x − 63x = 54 − 48

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Present age of A = 7 × 6 = 42 years.

⇒ Present age of C = 42 + 10 = 52 years.

Therefore, the present age of C is 52 years, which matches Option (4).

∴ The correct answer is 52 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The mathematical difference between the ages of two individuals remains the same regardless of how many years pass (Difference = A − B = constant).

Ratio Balancing

If the difference between ratio parts is not initially equal, multiply the ratios by the difference of the opposite ratio parts to balance them.

Future Age Formula

If the present age is P, then the age after n years is P + n and the age n years ago was P − n.

questions.question: The average score of 40 students in a class test is 45. Later on, it was found that at two places 25 was read as 35 and at one place 38 was read as 32. What is the actual average score of the class?
questions.questionHtml: The average score of 40 students in a class test is 45. Later on, it was found that at two places 25 was read as 35 and at one place 38 was read as 32. What is the actual average score of the class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net change in sum = (Correct values) − (Incorrect values)

Net change = [(25 × 2) + 38] − [(35 × 2) + 32] = 88 − 102 = −14

Change in average = Net change ÷ Total students = −14 ÷ 40 = −0.35

Actual average = Original average + Change = 45 − 0.35 = 44.65

∴ The correct answer is 44.65.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students = 40

Initial average = 45

Incorrect readings: 35 (twice), 32 (once)

Correct readings: 25 (twice), 38 (once)

Calculations:

⇒ Total sum = Average × Number of students = 45 × 40 = 1800

⇒ Sum of incorrect values = (35 × 2) + 32 = 70 + 32 = 102

⇒ Sum of correct values = (25 × 2) + 38 = 50 + 38 = 88

⇒ Corrected total sum = 1800 − 102 + 88

⇒ Corrected total sum = 1800 − 14 = 1786

⇒ Actual average = 1786 ÷ 40

⇒ Actual average = 44.65

∴ The correct answer is 44.65.

Additional Information

Average Correction Formula

Correct Average = Observed Average + [(Total Correct Value − Total Incorrect Value) ÷ Number of Items].

Effect of Constant on Average

If every observation is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the average also increases or decreases by 'k'.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A1 and A2 and sizes n1 and n2 are combined, the new average = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Hinglish

  • No one, nobody, nothing और nowhere indefinite pronouns हैं।

  • इसलिए बहुवचन क्रिया 'are' के स्थान पर एकवचन क्रिया 'is' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.question: Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. In some cases, the problem of the lowering of the river bottom has caused the water table of the surrounding area to drop, which has adversely affected agriculture. B. Also, another problem, canalization with its extensive system of locks and navigation dams, often seriously disrupts riverine ecosystems. C. The ever-increasing exploitation of rivers has given rise to a variety of problems. D. Further, extensive commercial navigation of rivers has resulted in much artificial improvement of natural channels, including increasing the depth of the channels to permit passage of larger vessels.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. In some cases, the problem of the lowering of the river bottom has caused the water table of the surrounding area to drop, which has adversely affected agriculture.

B. Also, another problem, canalization with its extensive system of locks and navigation dams, often seriously disrupts riverine ecosystems.

C. The ever-increasing exploitation of rivers has given rise to a variety of problems.

D. Further, extensive commercial navigation of rivers has resulted in much artificial improvement of natural channels, including increasing the depth of the channels to permit passage of larger vessels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CABD'.

Key Points

  • The sentence 'C' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "a variety of problems occurring due to exploitation of rivers". Hence, 'C' is the first part.
  • Sentence A will come after C because it introduces one of the problems i.e. the lowering of the river bottom has affected agriculture.
  • Sentence B will come after A because it explains the next problem i.e. canalization seriously disrupts riverine ecosystems.
  • The sentence 'D' is the concluding part because it further explains the advantage of extensive commercial navigation of rivers.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: The ever-increasing exploitation of rivers has given rise to a variety of problems. In some cases, the problem of the lowering of the river bottom has caused the water table of the surrounding area to drop, which has adversely affected agriculture. Also, another problem, canalization with its extensive system of locks and navigation dams, often seriously disrupts riverine ecosystems. Further, extensive commercial navigation of rivers has resulted in much artificial improvement of natural channels, including increasing the depth of the channels to permit passage of larger vessels.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
       

Hinglish

  • वाक्य 'C' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "नदियों के शोषण के कारण होने वाली विभिन्न समस्याओं" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः 'C' पहला भाग है।
  • वाक्य A, C के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह कई समस्याओं में से एक का परिचय देता है यानी नदी के तल के नीचे जाने से कृषि प्रभावित हुई है।
  • वाक्य B, A के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह अगली समस्या की व्याख्या करता है यानी नहरीकरण गंभीर रूप से नदी के पारिस्थितिक तंत्र को बाधित करता है।
  • वाक्य 'D' समापन भाग है क्योंकि यह आगे नदियों के व्यापक वाणिज्यिक नेविगेशन के लाभ की व्याख्या करता है।

questions.question: Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. “I will work hard to get the first rank in class,” said Rohan.

Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

“I will work hard to get the first rank in class,” said Rohan.

options.text: Rohan said that he could work hard to get the first rank in class.
options.html: Rohan said that he could work hard to get the first rank in class.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rohan said that he would work hard to get the first rank in class.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is a direct speech.
  • The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
    • The commas, inverted commas are removed, and 'that' is added.
    • The first-person pronoun 'I' becomes the third-person pronoun 'he'. 
    • The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (will) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (would) + Object'.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Additional Information

  • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-
    Direct Speech Indirect Speech
    Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1+ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject+had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य direct speech है।
  • Direct speech को indirect speech में बदलने के लिए बुनियादी नियम:-
    • Commas, inverted commas हटा दिए जाते हैं और 'that' जोड़ा जाता है।
    • The first-person pronoun 'I', third-person pronoun 'he' बन जाता है।
    • Present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (will) + Object' को past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (would) + Object' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
       

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. He win / several accolades / for his / music compositions.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

He win / several accolades / for his / music compositions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'He win' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the simple present tense 'He win' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is in the present perfect tense.
  • The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time.
  • This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.
  • The pronoun 'He' is singular, therefore, it will take the singular verb 'has' and the past participle form of the verb 'win' is 'won'.
  • Therefore, the present perfect tense ''He has won'' should be used in place of the simple present tense 'He win'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: He has won several accolades for his music compositions.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में, simple present tense 'He win' गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य present perfect tense ​​में है।
  • Present perfect tense ​​एक क्रिया या अवस्था को संदर्भित करता है जो या तो अतीत में अनिश्चित समय पर हुई या अतीत में शुरू हुई और वर्तमान समय तक जारी रही।
  • यह have/has + the past participle से बनता है।
  • Pronoun 'He' एकवचन है, इसलिए, यह एकवचन क्रिया 'has' लेगा और verb 'win' का past participle form 'won' है।
  • इसलिए, simple present tense 'He win' के स्थान पर present perfect tense ''He has won'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: He has won several accolades for his music compositions.
